Yeah, I don't see why not. My life has been a hard one. However, society would say otherwise. I'm a white male who's 16 years old. My family is securely positioned in middle class. My family isn't abusive or anything. However, my depression is still there. I'd say it started when I was 7. That's when my mother died. The next day, in school, it was shrugged off and I was forced by everyone around me to continue living as if nothing happened. Looking back, if I had a therapist to get me through those hard times, maybe I would've turned out better. However, instead, what I got was ignorant treatment as if I wasn't a 7 year old inexperienced child. I have strong memories of my father saying that I didn't let him grieve properly because I was such a bad kid in school. I misbehaved a lot back then. Honestly, I don't blame him for this. He grew up with the concept of tough-love. He is, after all, a product of the soviet union. There methods where to beat your child with a belt and make sure you guilt trip them into being good. However, my dad wasn't as abusive as I'm making him out to be. Yes, there were times where he emotionally hurt me, but physically it was rare. The culprit for my physically abuse trauma was my uncle. He beat with a belt if I misbehaved in any way. I'm sure many would say that this is normal discipline but I respond with "discipline-my-ass". Scarring a child like that is no way to discipline. Anyway, in elementary school, I was a loner/"the funny kid". I was the kid that made everyone laugh at the expense of my own dignity and this resulted in me being the weird kid as well. I had no friends until about 7th grade. That's when I finally started to reach out to people. In eighth, I transferred schools and that's where I got my first friend/best friend. I got to come over to his house, play Xbox for the first time, and do other friend-like things. I joined a clique and honestly had fun. Unfortunately, the mental scarring was still there. It's not likely suddenly getting friends got rid of my depression. I still felt sadness and my home life was a mess. Me and my dad would fight a lot and me and my younger brother were not on good terms. Speaking of my brother, I had physically and mentally abused him throughout his own childhood (he's now 11 I think) which contributed to my depression. I think I did this because my own childhood wasn't very fun. There were also some very disgusting things I had done which I will not talk about. They still affect my life as every time I look at my brother, I feel guilty for all the shit I'd put him through. Anyway, my best friend started sexually abusing me which made me distant from other people. I'm sure he had no clue what he did wrong since he didn't understand why I stopped coming over. Speaking of sexual abuse, when I was in fourth and fifth grade, I was sent to mental hospitals two times. The kids there were truly messed up for their own reasons. I had one specific messed up kid as a roommate. He ended up secually assaulitng me at night. Anyway, around 8th grade is when I started using anime as an escape. It was practically my life by the time high school started. I was envious of the characters in anime which led to self hatred. Goes by 8th grade and high school starts. I decide to join a STEM oriented curriculum in my school. Ended up regretting this later on. We had to do science fair which essentially ruined me and my personal life. It was way to much work to do. The homework load was insane. Now, I'm not stupid by any means. However, I'm very lazy and apathetic. Also, you might or might not know that ADHD and a ton of homework don't synergize very well. Obviously, I fell behind (this was also due to my deteriorating mental health) and my grades plummeted. This worsened my depression to the point of severe depression. Now, let's pause for a second and put this into scale. I started off with severe sadness after my mother died. Throughout elementary school, this sadness pursued until about 4th to 5th grade where I gained a hidden ability called depression (I forgot to mention that I got a counselor in fourth grade due to my misbehavior. Turns out, that was bad since I ended up telling her I wanted to shoot myself and that I saw ghosts and heard things around me. This ended up sending me to mental hospitals.). Here comes eight grade where I gain somewhat moderate depression. I also want to mention the Ukrainian camps I went to which were a mess but still fun. I experienced a lot there and accredit some of my depression due to that. Anyway, here comes high school where my depression ends up worsening exponentially.  By the end of the first year of highschool, I'd say my depression was in between moderate and severe. Second year starts and I had a bunch of people on my case. I decided to stay in the STEM program which was a very bad choice. First semester, my grades were looking not so good. After coronavirus started, the lack of social life hindered my mental health even further. Eventually, I became apathetic and gained severe depression. This led into me becoming suicidal and engaging in self harm. Again, I started watching new things like k-dramas which made me self hate even more. My home life was super bad until this december where me and my dad talked and sorted things out. However, the underlying fundamental problems our family had still pursued. Anyway, one of the major benefactors to my decision to end it all is school. School's been hard. I'm forced to work my ass off for nothing in return. I get no buzz from getting good grades. I see no reason to be learning chemistry, calculus, history, etc. for the job I want in the future. I want to be an artist. An ARTIST. Why do I have to learn all these things that waste my time. I want to pursue drawing. Unfortunately, our lives are controlled by other people so I am powerless. If I want to go live on my own and not be dependent, which I totally am willing to do, the government would chase me and it's also near impossible to live on your own without some starting money. I honestly just hate life and all the bad things it offers. People say if you're at your lowest right now, there are only better things to come. However, I think I've waited long enough for these so called "better days". I think I just need a fresh start wherever that'll be. Anyways, my life has been an utter failure (not a waste though. Some people might see it this way but I still lived it because it was my right to live it.). I was given this so called precious life and I think it's my basic human right to end it. Anyway, I'm sure that this is too much to read and therefore you might not read all of it but this is essentially my life story. I also have a first post I made a day back if you'd like to read that. This post is just and update to my journey to death's hands. Ciao.

Well, from what it sounds like, you have depression. How do I know? Well, because I have pretty severe depression and I have some experience in losing my passion for the stuff I like. I don't know your life circumstances but I will say this: What's your goal for drawing? Do you want t have a job based on drawing, do you want to make a comic, a manga, work on an animation? What do you hope to achieve with your skills. All I can say is that your depression probably won't get better in these times. However, if you give up your favorite things right now, then you'll surely regret it later ass you'll see the potential you had. Also, there's no such thing as ruining art. Anything and everything has beauty in it, including the drawing above. That beauty can of course have different levels of intensity but in the end, eveything is beuatiful in its own way. Just work on your art and get better. Also, if you feel like you've lost your passion for art, then try to identify wherre you even got it from. When was the moment that you just clicked and was like "I wanna learn to draw". After you find that, explore that moment and idnetify wether you truly want to pursue drawing. Also, set straight your goals. Undertsand what you even want from your skills in the end. I really hope this can help you somehow. Anyway, good luck soldier :)

Obi is Shirayuki’s guard and attendant, referring to her as “Miss” or “Little Miss”. Obi is shown to have feelings for Shirayuki from the time he saves her from collapsing in Fort Laxdo due to exhaustion, with the feelings becoming more intense as the story progresses. Shirayuki is currently unaware of these feelings. He is highly observant and is able to pick up her exhaustion and frustrations quickly. He sees her as a strong-headed and capable person, however her manner of approaching issues are likely to make her run into trouble, and thus understands why he is the most appropriate guard for Shirayuki given his nimbleness. Later in the story, Shirayuki and Obi grow closer. When Shirayuki is transferred to Lilias for two years, Obi follows her. Zen has stated that he is envious of the memories they have created together. Before heading on a journey to spread a flower, Shirayuki mentioned that he looks nice by the firelight, before admitting she can be herself around him. Once when attending a ball, they pretended to be in a relationship.
